options.label: 1. The Ghost Hand Floating Glitch
options.detail:
A live interactive test where the viewer stands in a doorway and pushes their arms outward against the frame for 30 seconds. The physical reflex causes their arms to float upward involuntarily afterward. This forces 100% retention as they must stay for the duration and comment their results.
Hook (en): Press your arms against a doorway now.
Why: Interactive physical challenges have the highest VVSA because they turn the video into a game. The Kohnstamm phenomenon is a reliable physiological reflex that works on almost everyone, ensuring high comment engagement with 'It actually worked!'

options.label: 2. The Troxler Fading Illusion
options.detail:
The video shows a fuzzy image with a central crosshair. As the viewer stares, the surrounding colors disappear. This is a sensory adaptation glitch that requires the viewer to loop the video if they blink, driving APV over 100%.
Hook (en): Stare at the cross; don't blink.
Why: Vision-based 'glitches' are currently trending on TikTok and Reels because they provide immediate 'proof' that your brain is lying to you. It triggers high 're-watch' value to see if the effect happens again.

options.label: 3. The Mammalian Dive Reflex Reset
options.detail:
Explaining how splashing ice-cold water on your face instantly drops your heart rate and kills anxiety via the Mammalian Dive Reflex. It frames a biological survival mechanism as a 'cheat code' for the nervous system, prompting viewers to save the video for later use.
Hook (en): You have a hidden survival switch.
Why: Bio-hacking and 'nervous system resets' are high-velocity topics in the survival science niche. Providing a tangible, science-backed 'cheat code' for stress encourages saves and shares.
